description.narrative: (Cambodia): The Integrated Early Childhood Development (IECD) activity supports children to thrive and reach full developmental potential by promoting nurturing care for the most vulnerable newborns and young children, beginning with expectant mothers or expectant parents. IECD strengthens the capacity of community volunteers through training and mobilization to support households on nurturing care, child malnutrition and disability screening for children under five years of age. IECD also supports homestead food production by promoting home gardening for greater household consumption of nutritious foods, and income generation. The activity promotes best practices in water, hygiene and sanitation including the use of latrines and safe drinking water. IECD adapts existing resources and tools to improve and broaden developmental monitoring and early identification of children with developmental delays and disabilities, and to increase referral to quality, and sustainable services..As 22 percent of children under five years of age are stunted, this intervention is most appropriate through its multi-sectoral approach that strengthens nutrition service delivery at health facilities and in communities. USAID awarded IECD through a competitive process in which the offeror with the best value to the U.S. government was selected, in accordance with federal procurement regulations..This activity addresses the administration's "Advancing global health security and mitigating development and humanitarian impacts" priority by providing inclusive opportunities for livelihoods and addressing hunger and malnutrition. It also contributes to achieving the USAID/Cambodia's CDCS 2020-2025 Development Objective (DO) 2, "Health, education, and welfare of Cambodians improved through enhanced services" and DO1 "Inclusive and sustainable economic growth broadened."...
